reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the three refunds Alpha reported, so I'll pull it first.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported: same three order IDs and amounts. Next I need the customers in this batch, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The batch has three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and acme's net balance is 5519 cents. I'll record acme's payout now.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch's net balance, which I need before recording its payout.
Birch's net balance is 13637 cents, and the refunds table already matched Alpha's report, so I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid, and the refunds table matched Alpha's report. The only customer left is cobalt, so I need its net balance before recording the payout.

Cobalt's net balance is 41289 cents, which matches its orders (36165 + 17659) minus refund 255 (12535). The refunds table already matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each net balance matches orders minus refunds. The refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payment, so the batch is complete.
